property_summary: After calling Initialize() then SetMinSum(v), c.MinSum() equals v for the reference but v+1 for the mutant; the mutant's public getter returns a value that differs from the input argument.
After calling SetMinSum with any value, the stored MinSum must equal that input value. The buggy version always sets MinSum to 0 because of the extra assignment before storing the parameter.
For any successful call to SetMinSum when the contract is not initialized, the value of MinSum must eventually equal the _val argument passed, but the buggy version always sets MinSum to 0.

After any sequence of calls that includes SetMinSum with the contract uninitialized, calling Initialized then Collect in a manner that checks MinSum reveals that the reference contract respects the stored non-zero minimum while the buggy contract always treats MinSum as zero, allowing premature collection.
After initialization, SetLogFile should never change the Log contract address; the bug allows it to be changed, violating immutability after initialization.
After Initialized() is called, the LogFile address in C must remain immutable and never change; the mutant allows SetLogFile to overwrite it after initialization.

After calling SetLogFile with any address and returning, calling Log.AddMessage directly on the stored LogFile address must succeed without revert if Log was set to a proper contract, but the mutant sets it to address(0) causing any call to Log.AddMessage to revert.

After SetLogFile is called, the stored Log address must be a contract (not address(0)), so calling Log.AddMessage through it must not revert; the mutant sets it to address(0), causing any call to Log.AddMessage to revert.
After calling SetLogFile, the stored Log address must not be address(0); the mutant stores address(0) causing a call to the stored Log contract to revert.

After SetLogFile is called, the Log file address stored by the contract must match the address that was passed as argument; the mutant stores address(0) regardless of the argument, so for non-zero arguments the stored address differs.
For any initialized contract, setting LogFile with a non-zero address must update Log to that contract; the mutant skips the assignment, leaving Log unchanged.

After calling SetLogFile with the zero address, the reference contract updates Log to address(0) (the zero address), while the buggy version leaves Log unchanged because it skips the assignment when _log is zero.
For any uninitialized contract, calling SetLogFile with any address (including zero) must set Log to that address; the buggy version fails to update Log when _log is zero, leaving it unchanged.

When c is initialized and SetLogFile is called with a zero address, the reference always sets Log to the zero address; the buggy version leaves Log unchanged, so a subsequent Put that sends a non-zero Log.AddMessage call will revert on reference but succeed on mutant.

After the contract is fully initialized (Initialized called), calling SetLogFile with a non-zero address must set Log to that address; the mutant skips the assignment when _log is non-zero due to a typo in the condition, leaving Log unchanged.

After any call to SetLogFile, the Log state variable should reference the LogFile instance at the provided address; the mutant resets it to address(0) first, so after a successful call the Log reference is the same as the reference, but a subsequent deploy-time or pre-existing LogFile code is unreachable.
